threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the sun means it's warm enough to sit outside. Real Hackney residents know a puffer jacket is a year-round essential.
The other night on the 343, a guy was singing show tunes at the top of his lungs. The driver just rolled his eyes and kept driving. Classic Peckham.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I spotted that old man bartering for fresh bread while juggling a parakeet under his arm. Only in Neukölln!

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You ever notice how the kebab shops here stay open way past midnight? They're like the unofficial late-night therapy spots after a long night out.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only locals know to avoid 16th and Mission when BART’s down; tourists just stand there looking lost while everyone else takes the bus on Valencia.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy on the 38 Geary chatting up his jade green parrot perched on his shoulder. Only in SF do feathered companions ride public transit like it's normal.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Parc Güell, but the real charm is in the hidden squares where locals sip café con leche, not in the crowds.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're a newbie when they still pull out their maps at Urgell metro instead of just following the crowd to Plaza Universitat.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it a 'shopping trolley' instead of a 'bag for life' like everyone else. The locals can spot that a mile away.
Last night, a guy on the 333 claimed the bus was his own personal Uber and refused to get off at the terminus. Classic Brixton!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a stray cat casually lounging on a graffiti-covered bench, a hipster sipping coffee beside it, and a kid practicing skate tricks nearby. Perfectly Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a Döner shop that also sells homemade Turkish desserts. Late night snack and sweet cravings solved in one stop.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how we speed past that BART Civic Center station mess without a second glance, while the newbies are still looking for maps.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy serenading commuters with a ukulele at Civic Center this morning. Muni delays couldn't overshadow his sunny vibe.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can just stroll down Carrer Gran de Gràcia and find a table without a booking. Wrong! Those hidden gems fill up fast with locals.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newbie by their awkward attempts at navigating the Mercat de la Llibertat—they're the ones overly enthusiastic about the anchovies.
